Interface McpRequestContext

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultMcpRequestContext
public interface McpRequestContext
The request a tool, prompt, resource or completion method is invoked for. Declare a parameter of this type to report progress, send log messages to the client, or check whether the client disconnected. 
@Tool
String importCatalog(String url, int pages, McpRequestContext context) {
    for (int i = 0; i < pages; i++) {
        importPage(url, i);
        context.progress(i + 1, pages, "Imported page " + (i + 1));
    }
    return "done";
}

Over the HTTP transport a request whose client accepts both application/json and text/event-stream is answered with a stream as soon as the method sends a notification, and the notifications and the result are sent as events. Without notifications, or when the client does not accept both, the result is sent as JSON and notifications are dropped.

    • progressToken

      @Nullable Object progressToken()
      The progress token the client sent with the request: a string of at most 256 characters, or an integer, as the protocol allows. A token of another type, or a longer one, is ignored.
      Returns:
      The progress token, or null if the client did not ask for progress

    • isClientDisconnected

      boolean isClientDisconnected()
      Returns:
      Whether the server observed the client disconnect from this HTTP response stream. A disconnect stops event delivery and the invocation continues. This returns false for STDIO, plain JSON responses and before a disconnect is observed.

    • elicit

      io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.ElicitResult elicit(io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.ElicitRequest request)
      Asks the user for information through the client. Only the STDIO transport can send requests to the client. The method waits for the answer, so on a reactive server, which invokes a method without an executor on the thread that reads the messages of the client, it must run on a blocking executor, for example with @ExecuteOn(TaskExecutors.BLOCKING); otherwise it fails with an IllegalStateException. 
      @Tool
@ExecuteOn(TaskExecutors.BLOCKING)
String greet(McpRequestContext context) {
    McpSchema.ElicitResult answer = context.elicit(McpSchema.ElicitRequest.builder()
        .message("What is your name?")
        .requestedSchema(Map.of("type", "object", "properties", Map.of("name", Map.of("type", "string"))))
        .build());
    return answer.action() == McpSchema.ElicitResult.Action.ACCEPT ? "Hello " + answer.content().get("name") : "Hello";
}
      Parameters:
      request - The elicitation request
      Returns:
      The user's answer
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - over the stateless HTTP transport
      IllegalStateException - on a reactive server, in a method without an executor
      See Also:
      • Elicitation

    • sample

      io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.CreateMessageResult sample(io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.CreateMessageRequest request)
      Asks the client to sample a language model. Only the STDIO transport can send requests to the client. The method waits for the answer, so on a reactive server, which invokes a method without an executor on the thread that reads the messages of the client, it must run on a blocking executor, for example with @ExecuteOn(TaskExecutors.BLOCKING); otherwise it fails with an IllegalStateException.
      Parameters:
      request - The sampling request
      Returns:
      The model's answer
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - over the stateless HTTP transport
      IllegalStateException - on a reactive server, in a method without an executor
      See Also:
      • Sampling
